topics.name: Athletics
facts: Athletics events are split into track events (running) and field events (jumping and throwing).
Track events include sprints (100m, 200m), middle distance (400m, 800m, 1500m), long distance, hurdles and relays.
Field events include long jump, triple jump, high jump, shot put, discus, javelin.
A sprint start uses starting blocks and the commands 'On your marks', 'Set', 'Go' (or gun).
A false start is when an athlete moves before the starting signal and can lead to disqualification.
In relay races a baton must be passed within a 20m changeover box.
Long jump is measured from the take-off board to the nearest mark made in the sand pit.
High jump uses the Fosbury Flop technique, jumping backwards over the bar.
Shot put is a throwing event where the shot is pushed (putted) from the neck, not thrown.
The javelin must land tip-first within the marked sector for a legal throw.
Pacing is important in middle and long distance running to avoid tiring too quickly.
Athletics develops speed, power, stamina, agility and coordination.

topics.name: Cricket
facts: Cricket is played between two teams of 11 players on an oval field with a rectangular 22-yard pitch in the middle.
The aim of the batting team is to score runs; the aim of the fielding team is to take wickets and limit runs.
A run is scored when both batters complete a run between the wickets.
A boundary scores 4 runs if the ball rolls/bounces over the boundary, or 6 if it crosses without bouncing.
A batter can be out by: bowled, caught, LBW (leg before wicket), run out, or stumped.
An over consists of 6 legal deliveries bowled by one bowler.
Wickets are made up of three stumps and two bails.
The wicketkeeper stands behind the stumps to catch or stump the batter.
A 'no ball' is an illegal delivery (e.g. overstepping) and gives the batting team an extra run.
A 'wide' is a ball bowled too far from the batter to hit and gives an extra run.
Wind ball cricket is played with a softer ball, often used for beginners.
Hardball cricket uses a hard leather ball and requires protective equipment such as pads, gloves and a helmet.
Key cricket skills include batting, bowling, fielding, catching and throwing.

topics.name: Rounders
facts: Rounders is a striking and fielding game played between two teams of up to 9 players.
The pitch has four posts arranged in a diamond shape, with the bowler and batter in the middle.
A full rounder is scored when the batter hits the ball and reaches 4th post in one go.
A half rounder is scored when the batter reaches 4th post without hitting the ball, or hits and only reaches 2nd post.
The bowler must bowl underarm to the batter.
A 'no ball' is bowled too high, too low, too wide or on the wrong side; the batter can run on a no ball but cannot be out.
A batter is out if caught, stumped at a post they are running to, or if the post they are running to is touched with the ball.
The batter holds the bat in one hand and tries to hit the ball into the playing area.
Fielding positions include bowler, backstop, four post players and deep fielders.
The backstop stands behind the batter to collect missed balls.
A match is usually played over two innings, with each team batting and fielding once per innings.
Key rounders skills include batting, bowling, throwing, catching and running.
